comparison: Perfect agreement on regional mapping data (C5, C20-C25, C28-C30, C35, C53, C55-C58). Both evaluations find the systematic survey across cerebellar regions with density contour maps to be clearly presented and well-supported.

Disagreement on M1-BPN pathway evidence (C6, C31-C33, C36, C38, C42). OpenEval finds the combined tracing experiments sufficient despite acknowledging functional inference. Peer reviewers find the evidence insufficient, requesting quantitation of colocalization and reproducibility data.

Strong agreement on multimodal convergence evidence (C3, C4, C19, C26, C27, C34, C37). Both evaluations affirm that the viral tracing and quantitative analysis unambiguously demonstrate granule cell multimodality and validate Marr-Albus theory predictions. Peer result also includes C48.

Disagreement on corollary discharge mechanism (C40, C41, C73, C74). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the hypothesis is speculative but plausible. Peer reviewers are more critical (UNSUPPORTED), finding the claims about automatic conversion to sensory coordinates 'not particularly persuasive.'

Agreement on uncertainty regarding functional interpretation of regional organization (C44, C45). OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental evidence for computational roles. Peer reviewers raise concerns about logical consistency with cerebellar learning theory, noting implications for independent signal adjustment.

Disagreement on the 40% convergence quantification (C26). OpenEval expresses methodological concerns about single annotator analysis and selection bias. Peer reviewers accept this finding as part of the strongly supported main conclusions without raising quantification concerns.

Agreement that experimental findings validate classical cerebellar theory predictions (C48, C12). Both evaluations affirm the connection between multimodal convergence data and Marr-Albus model predictions about granule cells mixing different modalities.

OpenEval finds the characterization of prior work limitations (C14, C15) well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological critique of previous studies.
OpenEval supports the inference about higher multimodality rates with additional mossy fiber sources (C69, C70) based on unlabeled dendritic inputs. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval confirms background claims about granule cell numbers (C1, C9) are well-cited and established. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background information.
OpenEval confirms fundamental anatomical features of granule cells (C10, C11) are well-established with classical citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates hierarchical organization interpretation (C47, C46, C77, C78) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative functional claims despite documented anatomical convergence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer reviewers request more characterization of transgenic tools (C50, C52), including specificity/efficacy of Slc17a7 mice and TCGO expression patterns. No corresponding OpenEval result addresses these methodological tool validation concerns.
